Kernel `ball_to_interval_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The smallest interval of `T` that contains the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$:

$$Z = [\mathrm{RD}(c - r), \mathrm{RU}(c + r)].$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval, empty exactly when the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is.
- $Z$ contains $x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line gives $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
- For a finite ball: $z_l = \mathrm{RD}(c - r)$ and $z_u = \mathrm{RU}(c + r)$, the roundings in the format with overflow: the smallest interval of `T` that contains the ball.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

## Source

**Algorithm:** the directed difference and sum of the center and the radius (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_to_interval_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_to_interval_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`sub_down_1`](sub_down_1.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

```
# The smallest interval with one-limb bounds that contains a ball with a one-limb center
# (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", "Midpoint, radius and the conversions", "Ball to
# interval"): [RD(c - r), RU(c + r)]. The whole line (0, +inf) gives [-inf, +inf] by the same two
# operations (0 - inf rounded down is -inf); the empty set (all NaN) is selected, by the test of the
# radius. These are the values of lower() and upper() of a Ball<T, 1>.

l  = sub_down_1(c, r)
h  = add_up_1(c, r)
ne = eq(r, r)
mi = neg(const inf)
zl = select(ne, l, const inf)
zu = select(ne, h, mi)
```
